themes.summary: Futures settled lower Nov. 10 as markets unwound geopolitical risk premium after Trump said new strikes on Iran were highly unlikely and crude fell below $90/b for the first time in more than two months.
CAS shows Hormuz crude exports at 4.4 million b/d end-October and 1.8 million b/d on Nov. 7 with 14 transits Nov. 9, while attacks slowed since Nov. 8 but IRGC reported two tankers on fire.

themes.theme: Middle East export and OPEC+ output recovery
themes.summary: OPEC+ output rose 2.82 million b/d to 38.09 million b/d in October and Saudi loadings hit a wartime high of 7.5 million b/d via Yanbu and SUMED routes.
Physical Brent fell to a $2.12/b discount to futures on Nov. 9, North Sea cargoes went unsold and Dubai and Oman cash premiums dropped back to three-month lows.
VLCC West Africa-Far East freight fell $128/mt m/m to $141/mt, easing arbitrage costs, while Treasury considers letting buyers acquire sanctioned tankers.
China October imports reached 9.92 million b/d, a 7-month high, though refiners buy hand-to-mouth and reserve buying is expected only below $65/b.

themes.theme: Agency forecasts keep prices elevated near term
themes.summary: EIA sees Brent about $100/b in Nov-Dec and $86/b in 2027 and CERA sees Dated Brent at $110/b or higher through end-2026, while JP Morgan estimates a 1.4 million b/d October surplus.
Talks in Abu Dhabi raise expectations of an energy ceasefire and eventual sanctions relief that could support Russian crude production and exports.
